outcome: breast disorders (palpable lumps, inflammation, persistent pain, abnormal nipple discharge)
cohort: 1248 pregnant women attending antenatal clinics at 26 weeks gestation were followed for six months postpartum.
finding: Women with a history of breast trauma and miscarriage were more likely to develop breast disorders during pregnancy and six months after delivery; benign breast disease, and number of pregnancies were also associated with breast disorder risk; while higher physical activity was protective.
